description: Per-resource metadata for owner review. Estimates are rounded to the owner's scale (10 / 15 / 20 / 30 / 45 min) and assume a first pass with the needed information to hand. They exclude any time spent gathering information such as quotes or measurements. Estimates for OG-B04, OG-B10 and OG-25 approved by the owner on 2026-09-22.

OG-B04.foundationTypeStatus: as deployed and approved 2026-09-22 (recorded explicitly so prep no longer relies on a MEDIUM-confidence audit value)

evidence.nature: short reflective planning answers: month, theme, why it matters, check-in day, what to share, partner, how to measure, baseline, target

OG-B04.reasoning: About a minute to read, then nine short answers of a line or two and a checklist to skim. Reused monthly, so the estimate is per month.
OG-B04.difficultySource: OWNER-APPROVED CLASSIFICATION — not source-derived. The source document does not state a difficulty level (searched for beginner, intermediate, advanced, difficulty, level, skill, experience: zero matches).
OG-B04.difficultyReason: 2 pages; approximately 15 minutes; short-answer planning activity; no technical content; no specialist knowledge required.

evidence.nature: budget burn-down with arithmetic (starting budget, remaining at days 30/60/90, a 10-20% contingency), phase breakdown, action dependencies and supplier lead times

OG-B10.reasoning: Short to read but the most thinking per field: budget figures need working out and dependency mapping means reasoning about the order of actions. Labelled Advanced, and assumes a plan already exists.
OG-B10.difficultySource: SOURCE-SUPPORTED — the document's own title reads '90-Day Implementation Roadmap (Advanced)'

evidence.nature: a brief for a tradesperson: project overview, resilience context, scope of works, commercial terms, attachments checklist, evaluation criteria

OG-25.reasoning: The longest document and the most demanding writing: a scope of works and commercial terms are substantive. 45 minutes assumes the member already knows what they want done; gathering measurements or quotes would add to it.
OG-25.difficultySource: OWNER-APPROVED CLASSIFICATION — not source-derived. The document states no difficulty. Its only use of the word 'level' is a form field, 'Target Resilience Level (Days of autonomy desired)', which is about the household, not the document.

OG-27.foundationStatus: PROPOSED — owner to confirm. Inferred: the roadmap spans water, energy, heating and shelter across three sprints, so it belongs to no single foundation. The audit's 'shelter' was MEDIUM confidence and is rejected. Matches OG-B10, its advanced companion.
OG-27.resourceTypeStatus: inferred, HIGH confidence — title 'Roadmap'; three phased sprint tables with owners and sign-offs
OG-27.categoryStatus: PROPOSED — owner to confirm; same as OG-B10
OG-27.estimatedTimeReasoning: First pass only: read the principles, then fill owners and deliverables for twelve weekly rows and note three sign-off points. The roadmap itself runs for 90 days; that is not reading time.
OG-27.difficultySource: none — the document states no level
OG-27.difficultyRecommendation: intermediate (INFERRED) — it coordinates budget tiers, professional bookings, consents and system installs over 90 days. Its companion OG-B10 is explicitly '(Advanced)', which suggests this base version is not.
OG-27.safetyReasoning: batteries-and-electrical: REQUIRED by the audit (solar panels, inverter, portable power station). carbon-monoxide and indoor-combustion: RECOMMENDED — Sprint 1 buys 'emergency heating' and runs a 24-hour off-grid test, which is exactly when people bring heaters and cookers inside.

OG-B07.resourceTypeStatus: PROPOSED — owner to confirm. Source-supported: the title says 'Worksheet' and the document is fill-in fields and a table. The audit inferred 'planner' at MEDIUM confidence from the word 'plan'.
OG-B07.estimatedTimeReasoning: Fifteen fields and a three-row shading table, with a payback calculation. Assumes the roof measurements, power bills and installer quotes are already to hand; gathering them takes longer.
OG-B07.difficultySource: SOURCE-SUPPORTED — the cover reads 'Advanced solar planning', the title is 'Deep Worksheet', and it asks for azimuth, pitch, kWh/year and feed-in tariffs
OG-B07.safetyReasoning: batteries-and-electrical: REQUIRED by the audit (solar, inverter). The roof survey asks the member to measure roof area and pitch, which is a working-at-height hazard. The safety standard has no block for it, so none is inserted; flagged for owner decision.

OG-15.resourceTypeStatus: inferred, HIGH confidence — title 'Scorecard'; sixteen scored questions and a total out of 80
OG-15.categoryRecommendation: heating ('Staying warm, including when the power is out'). The alternative is property-assessment; the scorecard's purpose is warmth, so heating fits better.
OG-15.estimatedTimeReasoning: A room-by-room walk-through: sixteen 1–5 scores, the hand test at windows and doors, and three short cold-zone plans.
OG-15.difficultySource: none — the document states no level
OG-15.difficultyRecommendation: beginner (INFERRED) — observation and 1–5 scoring, no tools or technical knowledge
OG-15.safetyReasoning: None REQUIRED by the audit (its thresholds were not met), all RECOMMENDED. Question 12 names 'fireplace, wood burner, gas heater, portable' as backup heating, and the page frames cold as a survival risk.
